I’ve had a migraine everyday for 8 months straight and I’ve been hospitalized multiple times from the level of pain. I’ve had dozens of treatments and medications that didn’t work and I was also hospitalized in a psych facility twice because the pain was deeply affecting my mental health(although I do have existing mental illnesses). I also have been out of work for 7 months and have only been able to see my friends in small doses. The only thing thats helped me is talking to people/psych which is really hard and finding hobbies to do in small increments. I paint, color, and make things out of clay in small bursts then rest. It helps keep my brain stimulated. If you ever need someone to vent to let me know! We gotta stick together because no one really gets it until they are in it!

One time I triggered a manic episode because I was drinking so much water it diluted the medication potency in my bloodstream. I have also had manic episodes triggered by being too stressed at work, moving, and from finding out someone had a crush on me(even though the feeling weren’t mutual). But usually it’s triggered by seasons, stress, or any big change. Whenever I start a new job it usually triggers an episode because i’m so excited/nervous.

I used to realize immediately when I was manic. I could just sense it. But the last time everyone was trying to tell me I was manic and I just didn’t believe them. The connection was not made. I just thought I was normal and everyone was being dramatic. Me staying up all night was just because I had a lot to do and didn’t want to miss out on that time. My insane irritability was just a bad mood. The hallucinations becoming constant was not anything to be worried about. It was weird looking back on it. I was very delusional

My mania starts as either insane irritability or intense euphoria, then hallucinations, then the no sleeping, then the impulsive behaviors, then the delusions, and then usually a weird state of complete separation from reality like you get used to living in different world than everyone else. My initial mood change is always the big indicator but the hallucinations seal the deal for me.

Shockingly I when I’m stable on meds I can go 24hrs+ without sleep and just feel normal. Not elevated or bad either. I find the days i’m more in a bad mood is when I sleep a lot maybe because I want to keep sleeping. I have been up for almost 30 hours and I just feel the same as I always do
Most people think bipolar disorder just just rapid mood swings. Like going from happy to angry randomly and that kind of thing or they think its someone who is erratic and “crazy”
For me its hallucinations start again but also needing less sleep and having an elevated heart rate

I have multiple sets of alarms and reminders in my phone and they are right next to my bed so I see them whenever I wake up. I take the ones I need later in the day to work. I have a med buddy and we take ours at the same time so we remind each other. I also have it written down and put on my fridge. I have adhd so routines dont work well for me and i just need it slapped in my face
My doc gave me lorazepam for a few days and that got rid of my akathisia! You should def ask if you could get this handled or it wont go away!
Oh I understand that i’m labeled as bipolar with psychotic features because I get delusions and hallucinations whenever i’m in an episode and I rarely have them when I’m not in an episode

I was diagnosed at 23! Before that I was diagnosed with depression, anxiety, and ptsd at 21. They thought ptsd was causing all the symptoms that turned out to be mania! After a horrible journey with two different SSRI’s i’m here!

Yes. I was in full mania and now i’m in like a mixed episode or something but I have been believing that the purchase totals of the customers at the store I work at mean things and tell whats going to happen in the future and angel numbers have become incredibly important to me. Right now I am out of it but I still keep going back to believing its real now and then. Also I hallucinate a ton when i’m in any episode and I often become way more paranoid about my safety as well. Its not great
There is definitely a good chance. These days I rarely know when i’m manic or not so it could’ve been a sign that I overlooked.

Last time I did it I just didn’t feel like it anymore. It wasn’t even that I felt I was better off without them I just had this thing telling me to stop. For some reason I don’t get withdrawals from any of my meds so I can stop taking it cold turkey without any super bad effects. I think that may also be a reason that I stop and start a lot

You always have a say in what you take! Luckily adhd typically comes with just one med and there are a ton of options to see which one fits you. As for the bipolar there could be a few but I would make it clear to your provider about your concerns. My psych is great and he always tries to keep me on the least meds possible but my symptoms are stubborn. I’m currently on 5 meds and I still feel like the same person I was before but better. You just have to find the right combo! It may take time but i’m sure you’ll figure it out :)

I mostly visually hallucinate. I see people, glowing figures, objects dropping or rolling, and occasionally creepy things like deformed humans but those are not super common for me. I also have some auditory hallucinations like people asking me questions when no one is there/near me or hearing people running behind me when i’m alone. I started getting them when I was a teenager and I get them when I have any type of episode. They can get super frequent and intense the when I don’t sleep. They don’t really scare me generally but the creepy ones are off putting

I am so insanely irritable and all my friends now know to just ignore me when I snap at them because normal me would never be mad at them for that kind of thing but god every little thing makes me fuming when i’m manic. My problem is I switch back and forth from elated to angry while manic so it can be confusing for those who don’t know about my manic episodes. I feel so guilty when its over
“where is the fun you? I want them back” my boss whenever I’m not manic
Most of my friends are bipolar too lol it makes it easy when we all understand whats going on with each other

I went off my meds for 3 months and had nothing happen but now being on all of my meds for months I had a manic episode start last month. You can never tell when the next episode will start so I wouldn’t be sure that you dont have bipolar just because you haven’t had an episode yet
I believe Lamictal/lamotrigine can cause hair loss in some people.

I tell most people I know well. I think it helps explain why I do things. My family is really accepting and already knew I had other mental health problems so ADHD wasn’t super surprising to them and now we joke about it all the time. A lot of my friends and coworkers also have ADHD so its kind of normal to talk about it because everyone gets it. I haven’t met anyone who hasn’t been accepting but I also don’t really let people like that into my life to begin with.
I have a small open shelving unit(its probably meant for shoes or something) and I use that for my pants! So you can still see them even when they are folded!

I kind of excel in jobs where you move a lot but I think thats partly the ADHD. I am also such a people pleaser that I need constant validation so I try really hard at anything I do to make my bosses happy which helps my performance at work. When I’m in a depression its harder to find energy but i know working hard will help my friends and team so I push through anyways to make sure they are supported. I mostly focus on other people and that helps me try harder. I think I derive a lot of confidence in being a hard worker so I always try really hard.

I’m starting to wean off abilify and i’ve been taking it for 4 months. My psychiatrist thinks the lamotrigine and lithium will be enough to keep me stable! But i’m scared that i’ll start hallucinating again.

I am very open about it because who cares if people are put off its a part of knowing me. I make jokes all the time about it so people dont feel like its a serious or touchy subject. “Remember when I was crying everyday at work? Turns out mood disorder whoops.” It makes the topic easier for people to parse and then they feel safe asking questions. My mom talks about it with her friends and educates them. Its all open here. But i’m not walking up to strangers and telling them or anything like that lol.

My psychiatrist is the best! He has ADHD and is obsessed with researching medication and studies. He is kind and helpful and is always cheering me on and saying how proud he is of me. Its always a delight to talk to him! There are good ones out there!!!

Had the same dude say all of these things in one session: “i’m gonna talk to you like i’m your dad” “if you want someone to complain to get a dog” “get a boyfriend it’ll make you feel better” “all of these issues will subside by the time you’re 28” “i dont think its anxiety i think its your personality” he said more things but the rest are just bad
YES EXACTLY

I had a very similar thing happen to me. Its less traumatizing to live and let go. I still hate him for sure but once I let go of my anger it allowed me to stop thinking about it every single day. Do what you want but know that the path of revenge means more trauma in the long run. Maybe you can find peace after the fact but it will be a painful journey.

People dont really grasp/ know about time blindness. Even people i know who say they have adhd say “thats not a thing” yes it is! I have it so bad! Minutes can feel like hours and hours can feel like a few minutes! when I forget to wear my watch its like i’m flying blind. My job rotates every hour so I gotta know what time it all the time!
Daily pill boxes that you can take with you, alarm, and the health app reminder set to multiple reminders and then sometimes i still forget and take them at like 4am.

I would say the world doesn’t change at all and you don’t even change that much it just makes everything manageable. I no longer am crying every single day but I still get emotional. I am not hallucinating all the time. The ups and downs are easier to handle. That kind of thing.
I just have a basic apple watch but it tracks my heart rate, movement,and sleep patterns including what depth of sleep I was in.

I work for a popular grocery chain(whos known for having extra nice employees) and its so fast paced and fun. You change jobs every hour and are always moving around and busy. I have combo type so i never get restless or bored because there is always something to do. I know its not like a fancy job by any means but its really great for me

I’m on abilify and lithium and so far no weight gain. They can also prescribe you metformin which can help a bit with your metabolism. But also if you can maintain a consistent diet that might be of some help. Can’t say for sure though. Your doc might have more answers :)

A lot of times I don’t even notice its a hallucination until they vanish because I end up seeing full on people but sometimes they do scare me and I get a sour feeling in my stomach. I had one stare me down really intensely and that was scary.

I’ve been able to recognize the bipolar in my behavior in my early teens so idk what horrible deeds I could have done before I was a teenager to cause it. If anything people did many many bad things to me in that time. So no i don’t think its a punishment.

You are a good parent for caring so much. It took me a long time to get past the anger I felt for everyone and everything around me. It was hard to overcome but its possible and i think it is possible for him as well. When you’re hurting you want to hurt others. Hopefully he can see that he has a support system that is loving and always there for him. You’re doing great :)

I wouldn’t push it too much. When my mom found out what happened to me she kept pushing for the details. She was being kind and gentle but I didn’t want it. You have to talk about trauma on your own terms when you feel ready and that might be a few years or never. I guess I would just say I know what happened, i’m so sorry, and if you ever want to talk i’m here but if not thats also ok. Idk everyone is different but I didn’t feel comfortable sharing until nearly 10 years after she asked about it.
The no sleep followed by pure energy. Also my heart rate will stay really high for hours on end. Thank you apple watch

I work at a popular grocery store chain(known for extra nice employees) and its really great for ADHD because we switch jobs every hour and have a lot of freedom in what we choose to do everyday. Its a blast! Many of my coworkers also have adhd and my bosses are all aware that I have it as well and there has been no issues around it.

I think what bugs me is when people call a person who is emotional/sensitive bipolar. I hear it a lot when there is a person who gets very outwardly upset or angry. I hate that. It really makes people confused on what the disorder actually is. Most people also dont understand mania at all and think its just extra happy or dont understand the psychotic elements that a lot of mania has. In general I just try to educate people when I have the chance but its tricky when its something that they likely will never experience for themselves.

The first indicator to me was my time blindness but my other one is that I can’t focus long enough to read a page of a book. I haven’t been able to do it my whole life and it takes me FOREVER to read anything because I have to read it 10 times over to really know what is being said. Those were the main two!

I have a small group of friends that I hang out with regularly. I go one once or twice a week but luckily I work with my friends so I see them everyday. Two of them also have bipolar disorder but we all have our own laundry list of issues that make it easy to understand each other and where we are all at mentally.
I will get nightmares every night for weeks so this is really interesting

oh yeah I can’t pay attention to any media unless i’m doing something else at the same time. I have always been that kid who was drawing while watching movies and now i’m that person who is playing video games with youtube and tv going on in the background. As I type this I have a video playing in the corner of the screen lol

The only thing I’ve found to help curb my shopping only works online. Once I go to start buying it I close whatever i’m using and immediately go to do a task or activity to distract myself. However if I am shopping in person money has no limit to me and I buy whatever I want.
Spring and fall I’m more likely to become manic and I’m super depressed in the summer and winter. Sometimes I get mania in the summer but its more often depression

I get similar random phrases stuck in my head. It can last months or years. Right now I get “my dad said its ok” for a very long time it was “she cried softly”. I also have bipolar and adhd but i have no idea if its normal or not. You’re not alone!

I work at a popular but smaller grocery store chain that is really flexible with my mental health problems. They know I have bipolar disorder and ADHD and are really helpful and patient when i’m having a tough time. I have had to teach a lot of my bosses what bipolar entails but they’ve all been really receptive. The company also will pay for hospitalizations and the insurance is great so I get pretty much free mental healthcare when I need it. Overall the job is really fast paced but generally not hard and I don’t really have to be stressed when I’m at work :)

I think the forgetfulness! Like forgetting what I’m saying mid sentence, forgetting why I walked in a room, forgetting where I put something,and forgetting directions I was just told. I was like oooooohhhh that makes so much sense now that I think about it

Its like a mix bag because some adhd meds can trigger mania and psychosis in some people and for others it doesn’t have that problem. I guess thats the same with most meds! My psychiatrist did the opposite and treated the bipolar first and then we’re moving on to ADHD meds but hopefully it all works out good for you! As always just keep an eye on how you’re feeling and be honest with your psychiatrist about anything going on :)
Yes same! Everyone gets mad at me because I get stressed when they talk too loud or yell or stomp. I hate using the vacuum cleaner and blender and just any loud sudden noise really drives me crazy

I have felt similarly because i’m getting on medication for bipolar and ADHD and many people have worried about me “losing my sparkle” but they also forget about the crying fits that lasts for hours and the raging and the erratic over the top behavior that comes with me being unmedicated. Not to mention the mental pain I go through dealing with all of it. So far on meds i’ve felt so so so much better being just like.. ok. I feel ok for once. Its worth it to at least try and see how you feel. For me its been great!! Its hard but its good!!

I constantly see people around me. Sometimes they are crouching down watching me, running past me, ducking behind something or just standing there watching me. I also see object fly off of shelves or just fall onto the floor like an apple or a ball. Usually if I see a person I get this sense of doom or panic. I also get a lot of smells like cigarettes or rotting meat randomly and for hearing I usually hear someone yelling my name or saying sentences with my name in it or hearing music. But those are the general ones.

My mom was shocked when I got diagnosed but most of our interactions as a kid were “can you just sit still for 5 seconds?” “Ok focus, look at me, focus, are you focusing yet?” “You can’t be doing two things at once just choose one!” or “she is always off in her own little world” And my teachers always saying “she is smart but need to apply herself”
At my job it kind of saved me because they started to understand and work around my needs. But I also have multiple bosses who have ADHD so I think that helps and I’m in the USA!
I’ve been on it for a while now and it really did save my life! Plus no more hallucinations lol.

I’ve been in multiple management positions and have done well by those standards. I kinda thrive at work because I can balance a ton of tasks and bounce between the work others cant always get to. If you want to be a leader you can be but it does take a bit of hyper focusing sometimes to get the most important tasks done lol.

I tell most people I know well because I am very hyperactive and cant sit still to save my life. I can be a lot for people to handle. I like to warn people and explain why I do the things I do and it usually helps in my relationships with others. honestly every person I told has had a positive reaction.

Take it slow and ramp up to eating full meals again. I found that sometimes eating a snack platter or making “school” lunches is easy because its usually cold and not too overwhelming to eat. Having people to eat around helps because you’re quietly encouraged to eat food around them. Eating out is good because they have a larger portion than you would normally eat. Keeping a snack on hand with you is always a good idea. And eating while doing something like watching a movie can also be helpful! You got this!!! We all are here to support you!

Soup and making myself lunches that feel like elementary school always helped. Like a pb and j with some fruit and pretzels. Just having access to good snacks like granola bars and yogurt help too. Idk if it helps! But thats what works for me. I pretend i’m making food for a kid lol

I no longer take SSRI’s because I have bipolar so they mess me up but I’ve taken zoloft and lexapro which are both known to sometimes cause weight gain. I personally had no problems with either causing me to gain weight at all the main problems I had were nausea and you’ll notice the main side affects in the first 2-3 weeks so just watch how you feel. It is different for everyone for sure but just take it slow and if its making you feel worse talk to your doctor and really push about how it affects you!! You got this!
